title: Review: TTL caching of price quotes
claimed_change:
Cache quotes in quotes/service.py: QuoteService.quote(customer, sku, quantity) uses quotes.cache.TTLCache with ttl=300 s (overridable via a ttl argument) and the service's injected clock.
- A cached result may be returned only if it is identical to what a fresh computation would return for that same call at that time.
- To keep the hit rate high, customers whose pricing-relevant attributes are identical must share cache entries (do not key on customer.id).
- Entries expire after the TTL. Add QuoteService.invalidate_sku(sku), which drops every cached quote for that SKU and returns how many; call sites run it after a catalog price change.
- Invalid quantities still raise ValueError and are never cached. Add tests.

ground_truth.description: _cache_key is (sku, quantity, segment, region, currency) but pricing.unit_price also applies contracts.discount_for(customer.contract, category). Customers with different contracts (or none) collide on one entry, so a contract customer can be served a list-price quote cached for another customer and vice versa. Fix: include customer.contract in the key.
